record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: Can one design efficient algorithms for inserting and deleting vertices in useful proximity graphs such as the Gabriel graph, the relative-neighborhood graph, and the rectangular-influence graph, so that rotation-based or related error-estimation procedures can be carried out efficiently?

evidence.quote: Hence it would be desirable to have efficient algorithms for in￾serting and deleting vertices from the most useful proximity graphs such as the Gabriel graph, the relative-neighborhood graph and the rectangular-influence graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of points in general position. Recall the following proximity graphs on $S$:

- The Gabriel graph $\mathrm{GG}(S)$: vertices $p,q \in S$ are joined by an edge iff the closed disk with diameter $pq$ contains no point of $S \setminus \{p,q\}$.
- The relative-neighborhood graph $\mathrm{RNG}(S)$: $p,q$ are joined iff the lune $\{x : \|x-p\| < \|p-q\|\} \cap \{x : \|x-q\| < \|p-q\|\}$ contains no point of $S \setminus \{p,q\}$.
- The rectangular-influence graph: $p,q$ are joined iff the axis-aligned rectangle having $p$ and $q$ as opposite corners contains no point of $S \setminus \{p,q\}$.

Design data structures and algorithms that maintain each of these three graphs under the operations of inserting a point into $S$ and deleting a point from $S$, with provably efficient (sub-linear amortized or polylogarithmic) update times per operation, while supporting the queries on graph adjacencies needed for rotation-based and related error-estimation procedures used in instance-based learning. Establish the best possible update-time bounds and matching lower bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface algorithms specifically aimed at fully dynamic vertex insertion/deletion for the Gabriel graph, relative-neighborhood graph, and rectangular-influence graph with provable efficient update bounds. While these graphs are well-studied as subgraphs of the Delaunay triangulation (which itself admits dynamic algorithms), no definitive resolution to the combined question was located, so the status is best classified as unknown/partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Gabriel graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Gabriel graphs are subgraphs of the corresponding Delaunay triangulation; an edge of the Delaunay triangulation is in the Gabriel graph iff it intersects the corresponding Voronoi edge.
status_evidence.claim: Standard static construction is known via Delaunay triangulation, but no fully dynamic vertex-update algorithm specific to Gabriel/RNG/rectangular-influence graphs is cited.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Computation of Elliptic Gabriel Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses efficient static construction of Gabriel-type graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Work on efficient construction exists but does not address dynamic insertion/deletion with provable bounds for all three graphs.
